research_rationale: Identity: Executive Order 12101 of November 17, 1978 (43 FR 54195, FR Doc. 78-32799), held at the official Federal Register text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12101.txt. Its single paragraph designates and empowers the Secretary of State to perform, without the approval, ratification, or other action of the President, the functions vested or to be vested in the President by sections 4 and 6 of the Diplomatic Relations Act (92 Stat. 809; 22 U.S.C. 254c and 254e). Later instrument: Executive Order 12608 (September 9, 1987, 52 FR 34617), section 29, amends this order by deleting the words for sections 4 and 6 and inserting the words for Section 4 of the Diplomatic Relations Act (22 U.S.C. 254c). That strike-and-insert amendment is listed as a later event; under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on strike-and-insert amendments the clause continues, amended, so the delegation now covers section 4 only and the section 6 function (22 U.S.C. 254e) left the order on the date of the amendment. EO 12608 states no separate effective date for section 29, so the date used is its signing date, September 9, 1987. Ending search: the order has no duration, condition or sunset. The held corpus was searched for the number 12101: the only instrument that acts on this order is EO 12608 (the 1989 Office of the Federal Register codification line, the Federal Register notice 2024-19192 and the U.S. Code note recite the order as amended by EO 12608 and do not revoke it). Current predicate: the held U.S. Code note under 22 U.S.C. 254c (release point 119-121, jobs/current-law/output/usc-notes) still prints the order as amended by EO 12608, and 22 U.S.C. 254c (section 4 of the Act) remains in the Code. It rests on sections 212(f) and 215(a)(1) of the Immigration and Nationality Act and 3 U.S.C. 301. Fourteen machine clauses cover it: the recital; section 1 lead-in; 1(a)(i) and 1(a)(ii) (Attorney General custody, facilities and screening); 1(b) (Secretary of State); 1(c)(i) and 1(c)(ii) (Secretary of Defense); section 2 (definition of mass migration); and section 3 (scope) with paragraphs (a) to (e). The inventory is confirmed without correction. Later instrument: Executive Order 13286 of February 28, 2003 (68 FR 10619, March 5, 2003), section 1, amends Executive Order 13276 by striking The Attorney General and the Attorney General wherever they appear in section 1 and inserting the Secretary of Homeland Security; its section 92 provides that it becomes effective on March 1, 2003, so that date is used rather than the signing date. Under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on strike-and-insert amendments the affected clauses continue, amended, with the Secretary of Homeland Security as actor in place of the Attorney General. The words appear in 1(a)(i), 1(a)(ii), 1(b), 1(c)(i) and 1(c)(ii); the section 1 lead-in, the recital and sections 2 and 3 name no Attorney General and are unchanged. The dossier's chain entry attributing a 1995 date to Executive Order 12977 for this amendment is a mislabelled copy of the Executive Order 13286 text and is not used. Ending search: the order has no sunset, duration or terminating condition. The held corpus was searched for the number 13276: the only instrument that acts on it is Executive Order 13286. Presidential memoranda published at 82 FR 48875 (2017) and 90 FR 38913 (August 12, 2025) each state that the memorandum does not affect Executive Order 12807 or Executive Order 13276, which shows the order treated as in force in 2025 and is not an amendment or ending. Executive Order 12807 is cited in sections 1(c)(ii) and 3(a) of this order as a separate order and is not held as revoked. Current predicate: the U.S. Code note under 8 U.S.C. 1182 (release point 119-121, in the packet) prints the order as amended by Executive Order 13286 section 1 with the Secretary of Homeland Security in place of the Attorney General; 32 CFR 245.9 (eCFR, amended through 2026-08-17, in the packet as CURRENT:EO:13276#1) lists it among authorities; the statutes it cites (8 U.S.C. 1182(f), 8 U.S.C. 1185(a)(1) and 3 U.S.C. 301) remain in the Code. Bounded searches read against their coverage notes: current-law:usc (release point 119-121, current through 2026-10-09; laws enacted 2026-10-10 through 2026-10-14 are not reflected), current-law:ecfr (eCFR as of 2026-10-14 and GovInfo CFR bulk XML; one hit, 32 CFR 245.9) and later-events:ofr_catalog (two hits, both Executive Order 13286). Limit disclosed: the 2025 memorandum is a recital, not a source for how any clause was applied after 2003; the claim rests on the absence of any ending instrument and the order's indefinite term.

earlier_end_check: The order's own text states no duration, sunset or condition. Executive Order 13286 section 1 substitutes the Secretary of Homeland Security for the Attorney General in section 1 and revokes nothing in this order. No other held instrument acts on it; the 2017 and 2025 Presidential memoranda expressly leave it unaffected.

The custody, facility, screening, resettlement and support duties are conditional or standing (may maintain, as appropriate, in the event of a mass migration) and none is a dated one-time task.

research_rationale: Identity: Executive Order 12631 of March 18, 1988, Working Group on Financial Markets (53 FR 9421, March 22, 1988), read in full from the official Federal Register text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12631.txt. It establishes the Working Group (Treasury Secretary as chairman, with the Federal Reserve Board, SEC and CFTC chairmen or their designees), directs it to identify and consider the issues raised by the studies of the financial-market events of October 19, 1987 and the actions to carry out the recommendations, to consult with market participants, and to report to the President initially within 60 days and periodically thereafter, and sets administrative support (section 3). The fourteen machine clauses cover the whole operative text without gaps and are confirmed without correction. Ending search: the order has no sunset, expiry date or terminating condition. The held corpus was searched for the number 12631 and the name of the Working Group: no instrument amends, revokes or supersedes the order. The later-events:ofr_catalog search has no hit for the order (no Office of the Federal Register disposition note names it as amended, revoked or superseded); the U.S. Code note under 15 U.S.C. 78b (release point 119-121, in the packet) prints the order as provided with no ending statement; the later held texts (Federal Register notice 2010-28177, the Presidential memorandum of June 4, 2020 published at 85 FR 35171, and Executive Order 14067 of March 9, 2022) refer to the Working Group as an existing body or to its prior work and do not alter the order. The one-time features are examined separately and do not end any clause: the 60-day initial report in section 2(c) was due 1988-05-17, a deadline and not an end, and the clause also imposes periodic reports without limit; the section 2(a) tasks carry no deadline and no held source shows they were completed or abandoned, so they are not recorded as ended. The June 4, 2020 memorandum directs the Secretary of the Treasury to convene the Working Group on investor risks, which shows the body in use after 1988, and it says nothing of ending it. Current predicate: the order is unrevoked and the U.S. Code note under 15 U.S.C. 78b still prints it. Bounded searches read against their coverage notes: current-law:usc (release point 119-121, current through 2026-10-09; laws enacted 2026-10-10 through 2026-10-14 are not reflected), current-law:ecfr (eCFR as of 2026-10-14 and GovInfo CFR bulk XML; no CFR hit for this order) and later-events:ofr_catalog (Office of the Federal Register disposition notes plus operative sentences in saved order texts; zero hits for this order). Limit disclosed: no held source shows the Working Group met or reported in 2025 or 2026; the claim rests on the absence of any ending instrument and on the order's own indefinite term.
savings_reason: No savings question arises. The order has no ending, repeal or revocation, so there is no residual effect to preserve apart from the continuing clauses; the bounded searches found no ending instrument.
earlier_end_check: The order's own text states no duration, sunset or terminating condition. No held instrument amends, revokes or supersedes it (held-corpus search for the number 12631 and the Working Group's name; the later-events:ofr_catalog search found no disposition note). The 60-day initial report date in section 2(c) is a deadline, not an end, and the periodic-report duty continues.
scope_check: Fourteen clauses cover the whole operative text: section 1 (establishment) and its four membership paragraphs and the chairman paragraph (1(b)); section 2 lead-in with 2(a)(1) and 2(a)(2), 2(b) and 2(c); section 3(a), 3(b) and 3(c). Each continues; none is recorded as ended because no held source shows an ending, performance or extinguishment.
independent_command_check: The section 2(a) tasks, the consultation duty, the reporting duty and the administrative-support duty are separate commands, each tested for its own end; the 60-day initial report is the only dated command and it sits inside a clause that also requires periodic reports without limit.
savings_check: No saving clause and no ended clause, so no residual effect separate from the continuing clauses arises.

research_rationale: Identity: Executive Order 11899 of January 22, 1976 (41 FR 3459; FR Doc. 76-2270, filed January 23, 1976), Providing for the Protection of Certain Civil Service Employment Rights of Federal Personnel Who Leave Federal Employment To Be Employed by Tribal Organizations Pursuant to the Indian Self-Determination and Education Assistance Act, read in full from the official Federal Register text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_11899.txt (the dossier's own-text boundary is verified for the whole order). Four clauses cover it: the recital (authority of section 105(i) of the Act, 5 U.S.C. 3301 and 3 U.S.C. 301); section 1 (the Civil Service Commission is designated to exercise the President's section 105(i) authority to issue regulations for subsections (e)(2) to (e)(4), (f), (g), (h), part of (e)(1), and other civil service rights it finds appropriate); section 2 (the Commission shall, after consultation, issue regulations, as it deems appropriate, on reemployment rights); section 3 (the Secretary of Labor is designated for the section 105(e)(1) regulations, except as provided in section 1). The machine inventory is confirmed without correction. Later instruments: (1) Executive Order 12107 of December 28, 1978 (44 FR 1055), section 2-101, amends and revises each order listed in it, including Executive Order 11899, by substituting Office of Personnel Management for Civil Service Commission and Director, Office of Personnel Management for the Chairman and Commissioners; section 2-404 makes the order effective January 1, 1979, so that date is used. It is a strike-and-insert style substitution, so under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 the clauses continue, amended, with the Office of Personnel Management as the actor in sections 1 and 2. (2) Executive Order 12608 of September 9, 1987 (52 FR 34617), section 27, amends the recital by replacing the statutory citation text for section 105(i); it states no separate effective date, so its signing date is used, and it changes no command. Both are listed as later events. Ending search: the order has no sunset, duration or terminating condition.
